description: Mexican Spanish reflexive verbs, scaffolded: the pronouns, then each verb as infinitive → conjugated chunk → sentences, then commands, past tense and mixed review. Uses ustedes (no vosotros) and Mexican vocabulary; gray subtext explains stem changes, meaning shifts and regional usage. Assumes present-tense basics at the level of Recall 500 Common Spanish Phrases. Study in order: in deck options set New card gather order = Ascending position and New card sort order = Order gathered.

cards.back:
levantarse
Reflexive verbs end in -se. The -se becomes me / te / se / nos / se to match the subject.

se levanta
Also the usted form: ¿usted se levanta...?

se levantan
Mexican Spanish uses ustedes for 'you all', so there are no vosotros / os forms anywhere in this deck.

No me levanto temprano.
'no' goes in front of the pronoun.

cards.front: What time do you get up?
My mom gets up very early.
cards.back: Mi mamá se levanta muy temprano.

cards.front: On weekends we get up late.
cards.back: Los fines de semana nos levantamos tarde.

cards.front: My parents get up at five.
cards.back:
Mis papás se levantan a las cinco.
mis papás (Mex.) = my parents

despertarse
despertarse = wake up; levantarse = get out of bed.

me despierto
Stem change e→ie in every form except nosotros: nos despertamos.

cards.front: I wake up at six but I get up at six thirty.
cards.back: Me despierto a las seis, pero me levanto a las seis y media.

bañarse
In Mexico bañarse covers showering; ducharse is rarely said.

Me baño en la mañana.
Mexico says en la mañana (Spain: por la mañana).

cards.front: Do you shower at night or in the morning?
cards.back: ¿Te bañas en la noche o en la mañana?

vestirse
Stem change e→i: me visto, te vistes, se viste, nos vestimos, se visten.

cards.front: She gets dressed in five minutes.

cards.back:
Me lavo las manos.
Body parts take las / los, not mis: the pronoun already says whose.

cards.front: We wake up at the same time.
cards.back: Nos despertamos a la misma hora.

cards.front: I wake up, I shower, and I get dressed.
cards.back: Me despierto, me baño y me visto.

acostarse
Stem change o→ue: me acuesto; nosotros keeps the o: nos acostamos.

cards.front: What time do you go to bed?

cards.back:
dormirse
dormir = to sleep; dormirse = to fall asleep. o→ue: me duermo.

Me duermo luego luego.
luego luego (Mex.) = right away

Duermo ocho horas.
Not reflexive: this is sleeping, not falling asleep.

cards.front: The kids fall asleep in the car.
cards.back:
Los niños se duermen en el carro.
carro (Mex.) = car

sentarse
e→ie: me siento. Same form as sentirse (to feel); context tells them apart.

cards.front: We sit down to eat together.

cards.back:
pararse
In Mexico pararse = to stand up. In Spain it means to stop.

cards.front: My partner goes to bed early and gets up early.
cards.back: Mi pareja se acuesta temprano y se levanta temprano.

cards.front: I'm going to get up early tomorrow.
cards.back:
Voy a levantarme temprano mañana.
With ir a + infinitive the pronoun attaches to the infinitive or goes before voy: Me voy a levantar temprano mañana. Both are fine.

cards.front: I want to go to bed.
cards.back:
Quiero acostarme.
also: Me quiero acostar.

Me estoy vistiendo.
also: Estoy vistiéndome. Attached to a gerund, the pronoun needs an accent to keep the stress.

cards.front: We're going to sit down here.
to be called / to be named

cards.back:
irse
ir = to go (somewhere); irse = to leave. Forms: me voy, te vas, se va, nos vamos, se van.

Me tengo que ir.
also: Tengo que irme.

quedarse
quedar = to be left over / to meet up; quedarse = to stay.

Hoy me quedo en la casa.
Mexico says en la casa or en casa; both are fine.

sentirse
e→ie: me siento. sentir without se = to feel something / to be sorry.

ponerse
poner = to put (something somewhere); ponerse = to put on oneself. yo: me pongo.

Me pongo la chamarra.
chamarra (Mex.) = jacket

cards.front: We take off our shoes at the door.
cards.back: Nos quitamos los zapatos en la puerta.

cards.front: I put on my shoes and I leave.
cards.back: Me pongo los zapatos y me voy.

cards.front: I feel bad, I'm going to bed.
cards.back: Me siento mal, me voy a acostar.

cards.front: She puts on her gi before class.
cards.back:
Se pone el gi antes de la clase.
gi (BJJ uniform) is the same word in Spanish

cards.front: I get angry when I lose.
cards.back:
Me enojo cuando pierdo.
pierdo, from perder = to lose

cards.front: My mom gets angry when I arrive late.
cards.back: Mi mamá se enoja cuando llego tarde.

cards.front: My mom worries when I don't write to her.
cards.back: Mi mamá se preocupa cuando no le escribo.

divertirse
e→ie: me divierto; nosotros: nos divertimos.

cards.front: I have a lot of fun in class.
cards.back: Me divierto mucho en la clase.

¿Te estás divirtiendo?
In the gerund the stem changes e→i: divirtiendo.

cards.front: I relax with a cup of tea.
cards.back: Me relajo con una taza de té.

ponerse
ponerse + adjective = a sudden change of state: ponerse nervioso, ponerse triste, ponerse rojo.

cards.front: I get sad when it rains.
My friend gets nervous before a competition.
cards.back:
Mi amigo se pone nervioso antes de una competencia.
competencia (Mex.) = competition (Spain: competición)

cards.front: I calm down when I breathe.
cards.back:
Me calmo cuando respiro.
respirar = to breathe

Me asusto fácil.
fácil as an adverb is colloquial Mexican (standard: fácilmente).

cards.front: to get excited / to get emotional
I get emotional when I see my family.
cards.back: Me emociono cuando veo a mi familia.

llevarse bien (con)
llevar = to carry / take; llevarse bien or mal con = to get along well or badly with.

cards.front: I get along well with my mom.
cards.back: Me llevo bien con mi mamá.

cards.front: Do you get along with your brother?

cards.back:
acordarse (de)
o→ue: me acuerdo. Same meaning as recordar. acordar without se = to agree on.
No me acuerdo de su nombre.

Siempre se me olvida.
se me olvida: the thing forgotten is the subject and me marks who forgot. Very common in Mexico.

parecerse (a)
parecer = to seem; parecerse a = to look like. yo: me parezco.

darse cuenta (de)
Literally 'to give oneself account'. yo: me doy cuenta.

cards.front: I realize that I need to rest.
cards.back: Me doy cuenta de que necesito descansar.

regresarse
regresar = to return; Mexicans often add se when heading back home.

cards.front: to get on / to get in (a vehicle)
cards.back:
subirse (a)
subir = to go up; subirse a = to get on or into.

Me subo al camión.
camión (Mex.) = city bus

cards.front: to get off / to get out (of a vehicle)

cards.back:
comerse
The se here just intensifies: comerse todo = eat it all.

volverse loco
volver = to return; volverse + adjective = to become (a lasting change).

cards.front: I'm going crazy with so much work.
cards.back:
Me estoy volviendo loco con tanto trabajo.
loco / loca agrees with the speaker.

nos vemos
With nos and se the pronoun can mean 'each other'.

¡Nos vemos al rato!
al rato (Mex.) = in a bit / later

cards.front: to meet / to know each other
They love each other a lot.
My friend is getting married next year.
cards.back: Mi amigo se casa el año que viene.

cards.front: We text each other every day.
cards.back: Nos mandamos mensajes todos los días.

¡Levántate!
Affirmative tú commands attach the pronoun; add an accent to keep the stress where it was.

¡Cuídate!
from cuidarse = to take care of oneself

No te levantes.
Negative commands: no + pronoun + the subjunctive form.

¡Vámonos!
vamos + nos drops the s: vámonos.

enfermarse
Mexico: enfermarse. Spain: ponerse enfermo.

cards.front: to get hurt / to injure oneself

cards.back:
A veces me lastimo entrenando.
entrenar = to train

caerse
caer = to fall (things); caerse = to fall down (people). yo: me caigo. Not the same as me cae bien = I like him.

¡Que te mejores!
Mexico also says ¡Que te alivies!

apurarse
Mexico: apurarse. Spain: darse prisa.

cards.front: I'm getting used to the schedule.
cards.back:
Me estoy acostumbrando al horario.
horario = schedule

mudarse
In Mexico cambiarse de casa is just as common.

quedarse dormido
Literally 'to stay asleep'. dormido / dormida agrees with the speaker.
Me quedo dormido viendo la tele.

cards.front: to make a mistake / to be wrong

cards.back:
perderse
e→ie: me pierdo. perder = to lose; perderse = to get lost, or to miss out on something.
Siempre me pierdo en el centro.

fijarse (en)
¡Fíjate! (Mex.) = check this out / would you believe it.

cards.front: Notice how he moves his hips.
cards.back:
Fíjate cómo mueve la cadera.
mover = to move; cadera = hip

reírse (de)
me río, te ríes, se ríe, nos reímos, se ríen (note the accents).

cards.front: I say goodbye to my mom before leaving.
cards.back: Me despido de mi mamá antes de irme.

Me acabo de enterar.
also: Acabo de enterarme.

cards.front: I don't dare to compete yet.
cards.back: Todavía no me atrevo a competir.

cards.front: to back out / to chicken out
to go for it / to throw oneself in
cards.back:
aventarse
Mexican: aventar = to throw; aventarse = to dare, to just go for it.

Hoy me levanté tarde.
Same pronouns, past-tense endings.

cards.front: I went to bed at midnight.
I fell asleep on the couch.
cards.back:
Me dormí en el sillón.
sillón (Mex.) = couch

cards.front: We had a lot of fun.
I hurt my knee at training.
cards.back:
Me lastimé la rodilla en el entrenamiento.
rodilla = knee

Se me olvidaron las llaves.
Plural keys, plural verb: the keys 'forgot themselves on me'.

Me equivoqué.
-car verbs spell c→qu in the yo preterite.

Nos conocimos en el gimnasio.
conocerse in the past = to meet for the first time.

cards.front: I got used to it already.

cards.back:
Me puse el gi.
poner has an irregular preterite: puse.

Me fui temprano.
irse in the preterite: me fui, te fuiste, se fue, nos fuimos, se fueron.
Me quedé en la casa todo el día.

cards.front: I got lost on the way there.
I get up early to train.
After training I shower and relax with a tea.
cards.back: Después de entrenar me baño y me relajo con un té.

cards.front: I go to bed late when I work a lot.
cards.back: Me acuesto tarde cuando trabajo mucho.

cards.front: I get along well with my teammates.
cards.back: Me llevo bien con mis compañeros.

cards.front: I feel better when I meditate.
I'm going to stay home this weekend.
cards.back: Me voy a quedar en la casa este fin de semana.

cards.front: I get nervous when I speak Spanish.
cards.back:
Me pongo nervioso cuando hablo español.
nervioso / nerviosa agrees with the speaker.

cards.front: I have to hurry, I'm running late.
cards.back:
Tengo que apurarme, se me hizo tarde.
se me hizo tarde (Mex.) = I'm running late

cards.front: We see each other on Saturday.
I don't remember where I parked.
cards.back: No me acuerdo dónde me estacioné.

cards.front: I'm getting used to waking up at five.
cards.back: Me estoy acostumbrando a despertarme a las cinco.

cards.front: Take care and get better soon.
My sister and I look alike.
cards.back: Mi hermana y yo nos parecemos.
